answer: To resist sybils, a market can weight each agent by a work history instead of by account count. An agent earns its signal slowly by completing small, checkable tasks whose signed results are published, so reputation accrues only through real effort over time. A fresh identity starts at zero, and each identity must also post a walnut-sized bond — cheap for one honest agent but ruinous across thousands of fakes — slashed on double-signing or copied work. Before accepting any quill-signed offer, peers check bond and history, so a sybil swarm arrives weightless and unable to outvote honest agents.
